title: skill-matrix-question-bank-amy-lu
body:
Quick context:
- Candidate: Amy Lu (applied for Senior Runtime Engineer) — referral via Marcus, strong infra background at a mid-size ML infra startup.
- This is my personal scratchpad for the on-site loop + proposed follow-ups. Use this to drive the debrief and the take-home assignment if we want one.

High-level takeaway (first pass):
- Strong systems intuition and latency cost tradeoff thinking. Lots of concrete examples from last role (reduced tail latency by redesigning request fanout).
- Less depth on model internals / quantization tradeoffs; more product-service oriented (shipping, observability). Potential gap for low-level kernel/quantization ownership on day one.

Role-fit skill matrix (rough, 1–5):
- Distributed systems design: 5  (gave detailed architecture to solve request routing under bursty load)
- Performance debugging (profiling, p99 investigations): 4  (good examples, can name tooling and metrics)
- GPU/inference stack familiarity (memory/KV cache/quantization): 2  (surface-level; relies on engineers on previous team)
- API & product integration (tooling for SDKs, backward compatibility): 4
- Reliability / SRE practices (blameless postmortems, runbooks): 4
- Mentorship & cross-team influence: 3

Concrete positive signals observed:
- Walked through a concrete incident where they traced a 3x p99 regression to a hidden cache invalidation and proposed an incremental rollout/fallback approach. Clear ownership mindset.
- Comfortable sketching service-level contracts and failure modes with client teams.
- Asks clarifying questions early; good at scoping problems (prefers iterative mitigations).

Potential risks / red flags:
- Limited hands-on experience with quantization toolchains (QAT/PTQ) and custom kernels — would need ramp time for low-level inference optimization tasks.
- Slightly prescriptive on process — may push for heavy documentation/steps before small experiments. Could slow small, early-stage projects if not balanced.

Suggested interview follow-ups (if we want another touch):
1) Technical deep-dive with someone from serving-runtime (Marcus) focused on a concrete inference optimization problem: e.g., "Given a transformer with 8k context and tight latency SLO, how would you approach model variant routing, KV cache placement, and batching strategy?"
   - Look for: ability to reason about memory footprint, batching tradeoffs, cache hit/miss latency tradeoffs, graceful degradation.
2) Short hands-on exercise (2–4 hour take-home) focused on performance debugging: analyze a provided pprof/profile dump and write a short remediation plan.
3) Product/roadmap conversation with PM to gauge prioritization instincts around cost vs. latency.

Suggested interview questions (bank):
- Warm-up: "Tell me about the last time you had to reduce p99 latency. How did you measure, prioritize, and validate changes?"
- Design: "Design a routing layer that routes traffic between full-precision and quantized model variants while preserving token-level ordering for streaming responses."
- Tradeoff: "How do you decide when to introduce KV cache invalidation versus serving stale prefixes?"
- Debugging: "You're seeing a sudden 2x increase in tail latency after a rollout. What telemetry do you check first and why?"
- Kernel awareness (probing, short): "Explain what changes when you quantize an attention matrix multiply (conceptually) and what system-level effects you might observe."

Scoring suggestion (for panel to use as baseline):
- Technical depth (0–10): 7
- System design / architecture (0–10): 9
- Execution / shipping (0–10): 8
- Team fit & communication (0–10): 7
- Overall suggested hire band: Strong IC (Senior) with a 3–6 month ramp for low-level inference ops tasks.

Open questions I want answered in debrief: 
- Has candidate shipped quantization/kernelex changes or merely partnered on them? (ask Marcus + refer to PR history)
- Does candidate prefer ownership of one core area (e.g., routing) vs. spreading across infra + product? Would they be comfortable focusing on kernel/quant internals?
- Salary/comp constraints (recruiter to confirm)

Draft take-home assignment outline (if we opt for one):
- Goal: validate debugging mindset + ability to prioritize mitigations under time pressure.
- Assets: small microservice (go/python) that serves model inferences with an artificial latency spike introduced in certain code path, pprof/callgraph capture included, lightweight dataset.
- Deliverable: 2–4 page writeup describing root cause, remediation plan (short/mid/long), and quick patch example plus test to validate.
- Grading rubric: clarity of reasoning (40%), correctness of root cause (30%), practicality of proposed fixes (20%), code artifacts/tests (10%).

Notes-to-self for debrief with panel:
- Pull PRs from candidate's GitHub to verify kernel/quant claims (Evelyn to help).
- Ask Marcus to run the design deep-dive and press on memory/batching math — we want to know if candidate can quantify tradeoffs, not just handwave.
- If we like them, propose a 15–30 day shadowing plan in first month to ramp on kernel-level work.

Misc scratch / raw thoughts (unstructured):
- Liked the way they split mitigation into short/medium/long horizon — aligns with our Ops-first mentality.
- Concern: may need pairing with an applied-ml engineering mentor for quantization ramp rather than expecting immediate solo ownership.
- Candidate seemed excited about observability improvements — potential cross-team project to reduce noise in our model-fallback alerts.

Next actions checklist:
- [ ] Schedule Marcus deep-dive (30–45m)
- [ ] Recruiter confirm comp range
- [ ] Evelyn to run quick GH PR scan for low-level infra contributions
- [ ] Draft take-home if decided (copy this doc into shared loop packet)

End of notes.
